name: Counter Rotating Discs as Sources of Vacuum Fields
description: Two regions of a known vacuum field joined across a thin disc. A displaced cut and reflection can produce positive surface density and two streams of ordinary matter circling in opposite senses.
convention: We use $G=c=1$ and the Ricci contraction $R_{\mu\nu}=R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.
history: A displaced cut and reflection join two regions of a known vacuum field across a thin disc. The cut lies clear of the singularity, and the disc's matter supplies the jump in normal derivatives [ledvinka2019discs]. Jiří Bičák, Donald Lynden-Bell, and Joseph Katz applied this construction to static fields in 1993, showing that "most vacuum Weyl solutions can arise as the metrics of counter-rotating relativistic disks" [bicak1993]. Their examples include the Curzon, Schwarzschild, and Zipoy-Voorhees fields [bicak1993].¶The two streams in a static disc have equal densities and circle in opposite senses with equal speeds. Their angular momenta cancel, and their orbital motion supplies azimuthal pressure without radial pressure [ledvinka2019discs]. The same Schwarzschild vacuum geometry can therefore surround a spherical body or form the two sides of a disc junction [bicak1993]. The global geometry includes the disc and the identification across it.¶In units $G = c = 1$, $U$ and $k$ are the Weyl potentials, with derivatives evaluated just above the disc at $z = 0$. The surface energy density is $\varepsilon = e^{U-k}U_{,z}(1-\rho U_{,\rho})/(2\pi)$, and the azimuthal pressure is $p_\phi = e^{U-k}U_{,z}\rho U_{,\rho}/(2\pi)$ [ledvinka2019discs]. Here $\rho$ is the cylindrical radius, and each stream has speed $v^2 = p_\phi/\varepsilon$ measured by a static observer. Positive densities and speeds below light require $\varepsilon > p_\phi \ge 0$, which also satisfies the dominant and weak energy conditions. Each stream's proper rest surface density is $(\varepsilon-p_\phi)/2$ [bicak1993kerr, ledvinka2019discs].¶Bičák and Tomáš Ledvinka extended the construction to rotation in 1993 and showed that these discs "can act as exact sources of all types of the Kerr metric" [bicak1993kerr]. Their discs extend to infinity with finite mass, and frame dragging makes the two streams asymmetric. In the local frame where the surface stress is diagonal, equal opposite speeds $v^2 = p_\phi/\varepsilon$ reproduce the azimuthal pressure [bicak1993kerr]. Ledvinka and Bičák distinguished this model, which requires radial momentum exchange, from freely orbiting streams in 2019; two circular timelike geodesics with positive densities impose additional restrictions [ledvinka2019discs].¶Werner Israel's 1970 seam occupies the disc spanning the Kerr ring singularity and carries negative mass moving faster than light [israel1970]. For the displaced cuts, the singular region lies in the discarded slab, and suitable choices of the cut admit positive density and matter moving below light speed [bicak1993kerr, ledvinka2019discs]. The character of the matter on the seam separates the two constructions.¶José P. S. Lemos and Patricio S. Letelier superposed thin discs and black holes in 1994 [lemosletelier1994]. They described their annular family as "the first known exact solution for a black hole surrounded by a realistic heavy disk of matter" [lemosletelier1994]. These discs have an inner edge and admit configurations without matter moving faster than light; their equal counter rotating populations have zero net angular momentum. A negligible disc mass leaves the geometry of a black hole with a disc of test particles [lemosletelier1994].

related.text: Israel's seam spans Kerr's ring and carries negative mass moving faster than light [israel1970]. A displaced cut removes the singular region and permits a disc with positive density and matter moving below light speed [bicak1993kerr].
Two retained regions of Kerr's vacuum geometry meet across the matter disc. The location of the cut determines the surface stress and the admissible streams [bicak1993kerr, ledvinka2019discs].
Schwarzschild's vacuum field supplies both sides of a static disc junction [bicak1993]. The seam's equal opposite streams carry no net angular momentum.
The Curzon field is a Weyl seed for a counter rotating disc [bicak1993]. Displacing the cut excludes the seed's singularity from both retained regions.

The Zipoy-Voorhees Weyl fields also admit disc sources constructed by a displaced cut and reflection [bicak1993]. The cut and the seed parameters determine whether the matter is physically admissible.

coordinates.name: Reflected Static Weyl

parameters.description: Reflected Weyl potential, evaluated from the seed at $(\rho,b+|z|)$; $U_{,\rho\rho}+U_{,\rho}/\rho+U_{,zz}=0$ off the seam
Reflected Weyl potential; $k_{,\rho}=\rho(U_{,\rho}^2-U_{,z}^2)$ and $k_{,z}=2\rho U_{,\rho}U_{,z}$ off the seam
Positive displacement of the cut, a length
Mass parameter of the vacuum seed, a length
Half length of the Weyl rod, a length

coordinates.convention: Coordinates are $(t,\rho,\phi,z)$, with $t$, $\rho$, and $z$ lengths and $\phi$ an angle. The two retained regions meet at $z=0$; the potentials are composed with $b+|z|$. Smooth tensor components apply at $z\ne0$; the surface stress on the seam follows from the jump in extrinsic curvature.
